subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Conductors vs Insulators
description: A quick, practical guide to Conductors vs Insulators.

hook.text: Copper carries current easily. Rubber blocks it completely. Why the difference?

buildup.text: In conductors, outer electrons roam freely between atoms like a shared pool.

discovery.text: Insulators grip their electrons tightly. No free electrons means no current flow.

twist.text: Semiconductors sit in between — they conduct only under certain conditions.

climax.text: Every circuit needs both: conductors to carry current, insulators to contain it.

punchline.text: Loose electrons flow. Tight electrons stay put.

quiz.question: Why do conductors carry current easily?
options: They are always made of metal
Their outer electrons move freely between atoms
They have more protons than insulators
